page: 🔬 The intradermal wheal literature nobody cites, and the two conclusions it overturned
sentence_as_it_stands: **Any measurement of injected local anesthetic damage to nerve fibers in skin.** The irritancy findings here are bleeding and bruising scored by eye. Whether repeated wheals cost intraepidermal nerve fibers — the damage that would matter to skin already depleted of them — has never been measured for any local anesthetic. The one measurement of any local anesthetic's effect on those fibers is topical: [dose figure omitted] lidocaine patches worn for 42 days lowered epidermal nerve fiber density in healthy volunteers, where placebo patches did not (Wehrfritz 2011, PMID 21530339).
quote: Furthermore, we observed no apparent loss in PGP9.5 immunostained peripheral nerve fibers in both the back and paw skins approximately 1 day after co-injection (Fig. 7). The number of nerve fibers in each optical field for paw skins, for example, ranged 18 –24 (mean ⫾ se ⫽ 21.3 ⫾ 0.7, in 9 sections from 3 animals) in the saline group and 19 –23 (21.6 ⫾ 0.5, P ⫽ 0.732) in the BLA-treated group.
corrected_wording: No study has measured intraepidermal nerve fibres after repeated injected wheals, and none has measured them after plain lidocaine with epinephrine. Skin nerve fibres have been stained and counted once after an injected local anaesthetic: in rats given a single subcutaneous injection of lidocaine with epinephrine together with an experimental adjuvant, PGP9.5-stained fibres in paw and back skin were counted about a day later and did not differ from saline (Wang 2008, PMID 18806059). The only human measurement of a local anaesthetic's effect on those fibres is topical (Wehrfritz 2011, PMID 21530339).
notes: The claim C046 sentence. The page does not cite Wang 2008 anywhere - a full-text search of the fetched page found no occurrence of 'Wang', 'bulleyaconitine', 'PGP' or the PMID. The same absence is restated in the page's own revision log ('Any measurement of local anesthetic damage to nerve fibers in skin' as having none), which would need the same correction. The repeated-wheal half of the sentence still stands: Wang 2008 is a single injection.

page: Comparing the injectable local anesthetics for intradermal wheals
section: What does each one do to nerve tissue?
sentence_as_it_stands: **Nobody has measured damage in skin from an injected anesthetic.** The one human measurement is of a patch: [dose figure omitted] lidocaine patches worn for 42 days lowered epidermal nerve fiber density in healthy volunteers, where placebo patches did not (Wehrfritz et al., 2011).
quote: Even though cutaneous analgesia lasted for several days after co-injection of BLA/lidocaine/epinephrine, we observed no tissue damage in the cross-sections of the skin surrounding the injected site. The epidermis, dermis, and blood vessels all appeared intact.
corrected_wording: No study has measured damage in human skin from an injected anaesthetic. In rats, skin was examined after a single subcutaneous injection of lidocaine with epinephrine together with an experimental adjuvant: the haematoxylin-and-eosin sections showed epidermis, dermis and blood vessels intact, and PGP9.5-stained nerve fibres counted in paw and back skin about a day after injection did not differ from saline (Wang 2008, PMID 18806059). The one human measurement is of a patch (Wehrfritz et al., 2011).
notes: The claim D013 sentence. The page does not cite Wang 2008 - a full-text search of the fetched page found no occurrence of 'Wang', 'bulleyaconitine', 'PGP' or the PMID. The section already carries two perineural rat studies (Kroin 2010, Yu 2019); this adds the only one that looked at skin itself, and the layers examined are named in the figure legend: The epidermis layer of the skin is shown on top, followed by the dermis, muscle, and subcutaneous layer.

page: Comparing the injectable local anesthetics for intradermal wheals
section: What would settle what is unresolved
sentence_as_it_stands: **Does anesthetic damage skin the way it damages nerve roots, or the way it damages cells in a dish?** This is the question the whole harm comparison turns on, and no study of injection addresses it; the one measurement in human skin is of lidocaine patches worn for six weeks, which lowered epidermal nerve fiber density in healthy volunteers (Wehrfritz et al., 2011). What would settle it: a study of nerve-fiber density in skin after repeated injection of several anesthetics, in an animal or in people.
quote: saline (left panel), control side; Bulleyaconitine A (BLA) (right panel), injected side.
corrected_wording: One study of injection addresses it in part: in rats, PGP9.5-stained nerve fibres in paw and back skin were counted about a day after a single subcutaneous injection of lidocaine with epinephrine together with an experimental adjuvant, against saline, and did not differ (Wang 2008, PMID 18806059). No study has done it after repeated injection, and the one measurement in human skin is of lidocaine patches (Wehrfritz et al., 2011). What would settle it: a study of nerve-fibre density in skin after repeated injection of several anaesthetics, in an animal or in people.
notes: The second place on the same page where the same absence is stated ('no study of injection addresses it'); recorded separately because it is a different section with its own 'what would settle it'. Only the single-injection half changes; the page's call for a repeated-injection study stands.

section: Whether the tissue shows damage afterwards
sentence_as_it_stands: Two studies looked for the injury itself rather than for its cause.
quote: Even though cutaneous analgesia lasted for several days after co-injection of BLA/lidocaine/epinephrine, we observed no tissue damage in the cross-sections of the skin surrounding the injected site. The epidermis, dermis, and blood vessels all appeared intact.
corrected_wording: A third study looked for the injury itself rather than for its cause, and it is the only one of the three that looked in skin: in rats given a single subcutaneous injection of lidocaine with epinephrine together with an experimental adjuvant, haematoxylin-and-eosin sections read by a pathologist about six days afterwards showed epidermis, dermis and blood vessels intact, and PGP9.5-stained nerve fibres counted in paw and back skin about a day after injection did not differ from saline (Wang 2008, PMID 18806059).
notes: The section's two studies (Bouaziz 2005, Kroin 2010) are both at a nerve trunk. The page's separate statement in 'Gaps in the literature: nobody has measured this' - that no study performs nerve fibre counting or peripheral nerve histology after REPEATED infiltration of local anaesthetic with epinephrine over days or weeks - was checked against the full text and stands, since Wang 2008 is a single injection; so does its remark that the field infers repeated-dose safety from single-exposure animal work.
